summary: Privileged session audit fingerprint mismatch and SIEM ingest timestamp normalization
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that privileged-session audit events sent to their SIEM appear duplicated with different microsecond timestamps and, in several cases, the per-session fingerprint field (session_fingerprint) does not match the digest shown in Redwood Console. They requested evidence for compliance review and need a reliable ingest manifest that includes normalized timestamps and a stable fingerprint for each privileged session record.

Impact:
- Atlas FS cannot reconcile privileged-session events with their internal control system; flagged as a compliance gap for their internal audit.
- Potential false-positives in alerting and post-incident forensics; manual deduplication required.

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC), prod cluster in us-east-1.
- Webhook delivery to Atlas SIEM via mTLS endpoint (atlas-siem.ingest.example.com).

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Atlas triggers a privileged-session export via console -> Audit -> Export.
2) Events arrive in SIEM; they see duplicate session IDs with different session_fingerprint values and timestamps that differ in microsecond precision after ingestion.
3) When comparing the event JSON against the console audit preview, the fingerprint value does not match in ~12% of sampled events.

Observed logs / payload examples (customer-supplied):
- Received event 1 header: event_id=evt-20260310-0001, session_id=sess-ab12, session_fingerprint=aa3f4c9, ts=2026-03-10T18:23:14.123456Z
- Console preview: session_id=sess-ab12, session_fingerprint=bb7e9a1, ts=2026-03-10T18:23:14.123456Z
- Received event 2 header: event_id=evt-20260310-0002, session_id=sess-ab12, session_fingerprint=aa3f4c9, ts=2026-03-10T18:23:14.123457Z

Customer request:
- Provide root cause and a signed ingest manifest that demonstrates deterministic session fingerprinting and canonical timestamping (microsecond-level normalization) for the exported privileged-session events between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10.
- Provide recommended configuration for Atlas' SIEM ingest to avoid duplicates and timestamp shifting during pipeline transformation.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Asha Patel (Support): Acknowledge receipt and requested timelines. Escalated to SRE for immediate investigation.

2026-03-10 10:01 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Reproduced a case where webhook retries and a downstream ETL in the customer's SIEM caused microsecond differences. Need to validate our fingerprint generation path. Assigning to audit-service owner.

2026-03-10 14:22 - Atlas FS (Customer): We see duplicates across multiple ingestion windows; some duplicates have different fingerprints, which prevents us from automated reconciliation. Requesting signed manifest ASAP.

2026-03-11 08:35 - Priya Nair (Audit-Service Owner): Found that in the export pipeline the session_fingerprint is computed at two different places: 1) export renderer (console preview) and 2) webhook serializer. In rare cases of concurrent session finalization, metadata race causes differing ephemeral metadata to be included in fingerprint computation.

2026-03-11 12:10 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Temporary mitigation: turning on single-writer canonicalization in export pipeline for Atlas tenant to force fingerprint calc at canonicalization boundary. Will monitor for 24 hours.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Atlas FS (Customer): Received updated feed; duplicates reduced but still seeing timestamp normalization issues in their ETL. Requested guidance for SIEM parsing rules.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Asha Patel (Support): Shared recommendations document and scheduled a joint runbook call for 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC.
investigation_notes: Checked audit-service logs for tenant atlas-fs between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10: export-renderer and webhook-serializer show diverging metadata at same event_id in 7 out of 587 events sampled.

Hypothesis: race between finalization step that attaches ephemeral 'last_actor' metadata and the serializer path. If 'last_actor' flips while fingerprint computed in two places, digest differs. Console preview computes fingerprint after finalization; webhook serializer computed before finalization in some fast paths.

Queried dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/audit-export-latency?orgId=1&var-tenant=atlas-fs shows export-renderer average latency 23ms and webhook-serializer path 19ms — timing overlap plausible.

Observed webhook delivery shows occasional duplicate HTTP 200s from SIEM endpoint during transient retry windows leading to double-write. Need SIEM-side dedup guidance: dedupe by event_id + stable fingerprint or by event_id + canonical timestamp truncated to microseconds.

Checked HMAC signing sequence for manifest: signatures stable. Will produce signed manifest for requested window using canonicalized fingerprints computed by audit canonicalizer (single source of truth).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: enabled single-writer canonicalization for atlas-fs tenant to ensure fingerprint computed only after finalization. This reduced fingerprint mismatches to zero in the 24h window post-change.

Produced signed ingest manifest for 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-10: manifest includes event_id, session_id, canonical_session_fingerprint, canonical_ts (microsecond precision), and sha256-hmac signature. Delivered to customer via secure SFTP and uploaded manifest checksum to the ticket.

SIEM guidance provided: recommend deduplication logic using (event_id, canonical_session_fingerprint) and a tolerance window of 1ms on timestamp comparisons. Also recommended idempotent webhook handling: treat 2xx as idempotent only if signature matches.

Permanent fix: schedule change in audit-service to always compute canonical fingerprint at finalization boundary and ensure webhook-serializer reads from canonicalized record. Planned rollout: canary 2026-03-20, full rollout 2026-03-27 pending post-canary metrics. Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-service/pull/459

Follow-ups: add unit test to prevent multiple fingerprint sources, add a monitoring alert when fingerprint divergence rate > 0.1% for a tenant. Assigned follow-up ticket INT-409877 for rollout orchestration and test coverage.
